message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection rests on the strongest coherent evidence package (endpoint + interpretable performance + study context). PGS003972 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is disease-focused and multi-cohort, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports a plausible full-model AUROC (0.69) with no obviously heavy/clinical covariates disclosed (covariates are listed as Unknown, which is a confidence penalty but not an explicit comparability red flag). Competing options have limitations: PGS001784 is from a pan-framework global biobank paper and its AUROC=0.868 is a full-model metric with many covariates (age interactions, many PCs), while its PRS-only R2 is only 0.0147 (so the high AUROC is likely covariate-driven per the provided policy); PGS002054 is from a portability framework and reports only partial-r=0.0144; PGS003429 is a screening/cost-effectiveness context with only full-model AUROC=0.708 and unknown covariates; PGS000753 is older, very sparse (29 variants) and reports only an OR=1.37 without AUC/R2; PGS003973 reports a high C-index=0.882 but with very limited context and appears inconsistent with other AAA models, with no PRS-only metric and only basic covariates shown. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and each reports an abdominal aortic aneurysm diagnosis endpoint (PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent; others are generic AAA). To select a best-supported model, I prioritized disease-focused multi-cohort development and PRS-relevant performance evidence over framework/portability-style scores. PGS003972 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis; many AAA-relevant cohorts) is a disease-focused multi-cohort PRS-CS model with a reported discrimination metric (AUROC=0.69) and European evaluation, aligning with the cardiovascular/large-vessel policy preference for modern multi-cohort exact-endpoint models. Competing options have key limitations: PGS001784 (Cell Genom) and PGS002054 (UKB portability paper) are framework/portability-derived; their reported metrics (R2~0.0147; partial-r~0.0144) are modest and not clearly superior, and the full-model AUROC=0.868 for PGS001784 is likely covariate-driven per guidance and not directly comparable as PRS-only. PGS000753 is older, very sparse (29 variants), prevalent endpoint, and lacks AUC/R2 despite an OR=1.37. PGS003429 is screening/cost-effectiveness framed with unknown covariates and only full-model AUROC/R2 reported, making PRS contribution unclear. Between the two Nat Genet siblings, PGS003973 reports a high C-index (0.882) but with age/age^2/sex covariates and without PRS-only/incremental metrics, so its apparent advantage is hard to attribute to the PRS; thus PGS003972 is preferred for more conservative, comparable discrimination evidence. Overall confidence is Moderate because across candidates PRS-only metrics are largely missing and several reported discrimination values are full-model and therefore not cleanly comparable."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (all are abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Comparing evidence packages: PGS000753 comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics paper (Million Veteran Program; Circulation), reports a clear per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a moderate external validation size (n=46,564). Competing models have limitations in the visible metadata: PGS001784 is from a broad ‘Global Biobank’ framework paper and its high full-model AUROC=0.868 should not be treated as PRS-only; its PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out R2 is small (0.0147) and it uses an extensive covariate set. PGS002054 is from a UKB portability framework and only reports partial-r (0.0144) without AUROC/R2. PGS003429/PGS003972 report only full-model AUROC (0.708/0.69) with unknown covariates, limiting comparability. PGS003973 reports a very high full-model C-index (0.882) with only age/age^2/sex, but without PRS-only metrics and with small validation (n=7,517), leaving uncertainty about how much is PRS-driven versus covariate-driven. Overall, PGS000753 is the most coherently supported disease-focused choice, but confidence is capped because no candidate provides a clean, directly comparable PRS-only AUROC across models and several reported discrimination metrics appear to be full-model rather than PRS-only."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All six candidates are direct matches on concept and endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo are abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA in each, with one explicitly prevalent). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Among them, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and EUR evaluation, which domain guidance prioritizes over portability/framework-style scores (e.g., PGS001784; Cell Genom) and over older sparse prevalent-endpoint models (e.g., PGS000753; 29 variants; prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on comparability of performance evidence, validation support, and study archetype. PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet, 2023) with PRS-CS and broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance for cardiovascular/large-vessel diseases suggests should usually outrank older sparse/prevalent scores and generic framework/portability scores when endpoints are aligned. Between the two, PGS003972 reports a clean classification metric (AUROC=0.69) but lacks covariate specification; PGS003973 reports a high C-index=0.882 but the metric is not explicitly PGS-only and is plausibly full-model, making it less comparable and potentially covariate-driven (even though only age/age^2/sex are listed). Other alternatives are weaker: PGS001784 is a pan-biobank framework score with modest PRS-only R2 (~0.0147) and a high full-model AUROC (0.868) that is likely dominated by covariates; PGS002054 is a UKB portability framework with only partial-r (~0.0144); PGS000753 is an older 29-variant prevalent AAA score with only an OR (1.37); PGS003429 is a screening/cost-effectiveness context score with only full-model AUROC (0.708) and unknown covariates. Remaining limitation: the PGS003972 vs PGS003973 choice is not fully resolvable from the visible metadata (unclear whether PGS003973’s C-index is PRS-comparable and PGS003972 lacks covariate details), so confidence is moderated and the overall outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm or a near-identical diagnosis endpoint; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on concept and endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo all ‘Abdominal aortic aneurysm’, phenotyping_reported is AAA or prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported (all are abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the trait/EFO level, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS004606 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: \"Age-related macular degeneration\"), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS/architecture paper (Nat Genet; IAMDGC development cohort), and reports a representative European validation with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) plus explicit discrimination (AUROC=0.71) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.76, 95% CI 1.73–1.78) in a large validation sample (n=163,011). Competing models include (i) portability/framework UKB scores (PGS001834/PGS002041) with only weak partial-correlation metrics (~0.016–0.018) and less disease-focused publication context, (ii) PGS002269 with phenotype mismatch in phenotyping_reported (retinal layer thickness proxy) despite AMD labeling, (iii) PGS004607 with lower reported AUROC (0.65) and weaker OR (1.48) in the same European evaluation, and (iv) PGS004952 which reports a much higher full-model AUROC but is for \"Late\" AMD with a very small validation (n=1,232) and has an internal inconsistency in the cataloged AUROC value (84.2 vs 0.842), making its metric less reliable/comparable from the visible evidence. Limitation: only full-model AUROC is available for PGS004606 (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2), so some uncertainty remains about how much discrimination is PRS-driven versus covariate-driven, keeping confidence at Moderate."}
